title: A class that owns its repairs

terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Build main.cpp and bench.cpp into one program here and run it.

tasks.title: Give the bench its repairs
tasks.description:
Inside `class Bench` in `src/bench.h`, under `// Task 1`, write:

- under `private:`, a `std::vector<Repair>` called `repairs`
- under `public:`, the first line of `add`, which takes a repair as a reference to a `const Repair` and gives back a `bool`, and of `all`, a `const` member function that takes nothing and gives back the repairs as a `std::vector<Repair>`

Under `// Task 1` in `src/bench.cpp`, write their bodies, each with `Bench::` in front of its name. `add` puts a copy of the repair on the bench and gives back `true`, unless a repair with the same ticket is on it already: then it changes nothing and gives back `false`. `all` gives back a copy of the repairs, in the order they were added.

Check builds a program of its own with your two files. It adds repairs of its own, some with a ticket already on the bench, reads them back with `all` through a `const Bench&`, makes two benches and a copy of one, and empties the vector `all` gives back to see that the bench keeps its repairs. It also compiles a line of its own outside the class that reaches `repairs`, which must be refused.
nextSteps: In `bench.h`, write the vector under `private:` and the two first lines under `public:`.
In `bench.cpp`, write `add`: look through the repairs for the same ticket before you add.
Write `all`, which gives back the vector: a copy goes back to the caller.
In `main`, make a `Bench`, add the two repairs and print how many `all` gives back.
hints: The bench owns its vector: no code outside the class can reach it, so every change goes through the bench's own functions, which keep its rules.
A function that gives back `std::vector<Repair>` gives back a copy of the member, so whatever the caller does to it, the bench's own vector stays as it was.

The shape is `for (const Repair& held : repairs) { if (held.getTicket() == repair.getTicket()) { return false; } } repairs.push_back(repair); return true;` and `std::vector<Repair> Bench::all() const { return repairs; }`.

tasks.title: Find a repair by its ticket
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2` in `src/bench.h`, inside the class and under `public:`, write the first line of `find`, a `const` member function that takes a ticket as an `int` and gives back a `Repair`. Under `// Task 2` in `src/bench.cpp`, write its body: it gives back a copy of the repair with that ticket, or, when no repair on the bench has it, a `Repair` made with no values.

Check fills benches of its own, calls `find` through a `const Bench&` with tickets of its own, some on the bench and one that is not, and changes the repair `find` gives back to see that the bench's own repair stays as it was. Check builds this task with a `repairs`, an `add` and an `all` of its own, written as Task 1 asks, so it is judged on its own.
nextSteps: Write the first line in `bench.h`, with `const` at the end.
In `bench.cpp`, look at every repair on the bench, and give back the one with the ticket.
After the loop, when none had it, give back `Repair()`.
In `main`, find a ticket and print its item, then a ticket that is not on the bench.
hints: `find` only reads the bench, so it is `const`. Giving back a `Repair` gives back a copy: the caller can change it without touching the bench.
A repair that does not match only means it is not that one. Only after every repair was looked at is it certain that none has the ticket.
The shape is `for (const Repair& held : repairs) { if (held.getTicket() == ticket) { return held; } } return Repair();`.

tasks.title: Total the bench's minutes
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3` in `src/bench.h`, inside the class and under `public:`, write the first line of `totalMinutes`, a `const` member function that takes nothing and gives back an `int`. Under `// Task 3` in `src/bench.cpp`, write its body: the minutes of every repair on the bench, added up, worked out from the repairs each time it is called.

Check calls `totalMinutes` through a `const Bench&` on an empty bench, and on benches of its own as it adds repairs with minutes of its own. Check builds this task with a `repairs`, an `add` and an `all` of its own, written as Task 1 asks, so it is judged on its own.
nextSteps: Write the first line in `bench.h`, with `const` at the end.
Add each repair's minutes to it, through `getMinutes`.
Give the total back, and print it from `main` before and after you add a repair.
hints: The bench already holds everything the total needs. A total kept in a member of its own has to be changed by every function that changes the repairs, and goes wrong the day one forgets.
Each repair's minutes are added to the total, not put in its place.
The shape is `int total = 0; for (const Repair& held : repairs) { total += held.getMinutes(); } return total;`.

tasks.title: Take a repair off the bench
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 4` in `src/bench.h`, inside the class and under `public:`, write the first line of `remove`, which takes a ticket as an `int` and gives back a `bool`. Under `// Task 4` in `src/bench.cpp`, write its body: it takes the repair with that ticket off the bench, keeps the others in their order and gives back `true`. When no repair has that ticket, it changes nothing and gives back `false`.

Check fills benches of its own, removes the first, a middle and the last repair, a ticket that is not there, and one from an empty bench, and reads what is left with `all`. Check builds this task with the library's guard, which stops a program that reads a vector past its end, and with a `repairs`, an `add` and an `all` of its own, written as Task 1 asks, so it is judged on its own.
nextSteps: Write the first line in `bench.h`. It changes the bench, so no `const`.
In `bench.cpp`, find the position of the repair with that ticket, with a counted loop.
Take it out with `erase`, at that position, and give back `true`.
After the loop, give back `false`. Try it from `main` and print what `all` holds.
hints: `erase` takes a position counted from `begin()`: `repairs.begin() + i` is position `i`. The repairs after it move up one place, so the others keep their order.
Once the repair is gone, the work is done: give back `true` right there, before the loop goes on to a position that has moved.
The shape is `for (std::size_t i = 0; i < repairs.size(); i++) { if (repairs[i].getTicket() == ticket) { repairs.erase(repairs.begin() + i); return true; } } return false;`.
